_note: Every on-demand practice's applies_to, with the reason, as reviewable data.
EVERY on-demand practice is listed, including the ones deliberately left at
'**' -- a decision to leave a practice unrouted has to be visible, not an
omission. This is the same discipline tools/section_split.json uses for the
'**' means the path channel never fires for this practice: it is reachable

GATES are the fourth loading channel: a named MOMENT, not a place. A practice whose occasion is a moment cannot be reached by a glob, however well written -- that is why 26 entries here stay at '**'. tools/precedent_gate.py loads a gate's practices at the moment it is reached.
through the occasion index, a gate, or a check, and the 'why' says which.
tools/verify_harness.py fails if practices/*.md and this file disagree.

THE RULE THIS PASS SETTLED ON, after two rounds of narrowing: a glob is justified only where the path identifies the practice's DISTINGUISHING condition, not merely a necessary one. 'A rule is being written' is necessary for volatile-rules-carry-dates and not distinguishing; 'a new rule is being written' IS distinguishing for cite-the-incident. Applying that uniformly is what stopped this pass from becoming a search for globs that make a number move.

acronyms-glossary.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.

affordance-is-shared.why: No locus. 'A mechanism that makes something reachable' is a property of what you built, not of where you built it.

build-buy-decompose.why: A decision, made before any file exists.

capture-gate.why: A moment, not a place — routed by the `merge` gate instead.

check-source-architecture.why: A reasoning step about options, with no artifact.

checkable-gets-checked.why: Fires when a new practice is written, same locus as cite-the-incident, whose glob this copies directly.
checkable-gets-checked.gates_why: Whether a check was genuinely attempted is a judgment a review makes, the same as mistakes-become-rules' proportionality guard.

cite-the-incident.why: A new convention or rule is written into the catalogue. That is a place, not just a moment, and its check already scopes there.
cite-the-incident.gates_why: A review that produces a rule produces it here; it also has a glob for where the rule is written.

code-cites-practice.why: The occasion is writing code because a practice requires it, which happens in tools/ -- this repo's only place code implementing a practice's behavior is written.

computed-numbers-in-scripts.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.

cross-source-rollout.why: A moment, not a place -- what makes a change cross-source-relevant is its meaning, not which file it touched, so no glob identifies it. Routed by the `merge` gate instead.

A first draft of this pass used tools/** and surfaced the practice on 10 of 20 eval cases against 3 it applies to; re-reading the occasion is what narrowed it, not the cost figure, though the cost figure is what prompted the re-read.

frame-from-audience-question.why: No path tells you who the audience is.

generated-artifact-provenance.why: Where this repo actually builds and commits generated artifacts. Narrow on purpose: a glob over everything a build might touch would fire constantly and say nothing.

github-setup-disclosed.why: The distinguishing condition is that the install step is GitHub-SPECIFIC, and the workflow files are exactly that. INSTALL.md and SETUP.md were in a first draft of this glob; they are where the fact must be DISCLOSED, not what makes the practice fire, and including them surfaced it on half the eval cases.

label-describes-content.why: Set at phase 1 from the Install text, which named a path unambiguously.

layered-practice-packs.why: Deciding where a new rule belongs happens where rules and the source declaration live.

lead-with-what-it-is.why: Phase 1 scoped this to README.md alone from the Install text, but the practice's own occasion is "writing a README or other project-facing entry document" -- and AGENTS.md's own Conventions section (readers-vocabulary) already names SETUP.md and templates/GETTING_STARTED.md alongside README.md as this repo's other outward-facing entry documents. lead-with-what-it-is.decided: phase 1, widened in the 2026-09-02 deep-check pass

scripts-assert-properties.why: No path locus, and a glob would contradict the practice's own scope gate: 'Scripts that own their own numbers end to end need nothing. Keep the instrumented list explicit.' That explicit list IS the routing mechanism, and it exists -- model_audit's INSTRUMENTED. A glob over tools/** would surface the Rule on every script and is exactly the over-instrumentation the gate forbids.

tabular-shared-renderer.why: Fires on publishing a table, which no path in this repo identifies.

variant-re-derives.why: Fires on the relationship between a thing and its variant.

reply-links-files.why: Resident; its applies_to is not this file's business.

repo-is-memory.why: Resident; its applies_to is not this file's business.

routing-audit.why: Not a place -- "checking whether practices that should have fired, fired" is a periodic act a person invokes, not a file-touch trigger. Reachability comes from its occasion clause.

full-practice-audit.why: Not a place -- a whole-catalogue sweep is invoked explicitly by a person, not triggered by touching any one file. Reachability comes from its occasion clause.

very-deep-check.why: Not a place -- a whole-repo coherence review is invoked explicitly by a person, or after drift-inviting work, not triggered by touching any one file. Reachability comes from its occasion clause, the same as its full-practice-audit and routing-audit siblings.

_note: The gate vocabulary is closed: tools/verify_harness.py refuses an unknown gate name, and refuses a gate with no practices. Each gate names a moment with a real invocation point in this repo.

gates.reply: ending a turn and writing the reply — the stop hook
